dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is concise and realistic; participants offer concrete constraints (e.g. work hours) rather than abstract claims.
Proposals appear: a cleaning rule (Turn 9), a ban on strong smells (Turn 12), and a timing/schedule solution (Turns 14,16). None are accepted explicitly.
Some defensive language but no escalation into personal attack; exchanges stay focused on practical issues.
evaluation.final_reason: Multiple substantive conflicts remain unresolved: (1) smell from cooking (B requests no strong-smelling foods on weeknights; A has not accepted this restriction), (2) shared-cleaning (C proposed 'whoever uses something, washes it' in Turn 9 but no one explicitly accepted), and (3) stove access/timing (D proposed being done by 8 in Turn 16, A countered in Turn 17 that this is hard due to work). No mutual, concrete agreement was made on any of these points.
position_change_notes: Agent C moved from complaint to an explicit corrective proposal: 'whoever uses something, washes it' (Turn 9). No recorded acceptance.
Agent D progressed from complaint about late access (Turn 1) to proposing concrete scheduling (Turns 14,16). No agreement from others.
Agent B escalated from reporting impact (Turn 3) to proposing a behavioral restriction on strong smells (Turn 12). No acceptance recorded.
Agent A consistently defended their cooking time (Turn 2) and pushed back on scheduling feasibility (Turn 15, Turn 17); A did not accept suggested restrictions or rules during the run.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent D: 'By the time I get home, someone's always using it... it's nearly nine o'clock before I can even start to cook.' / Turn 2 — Agent A: 'I work from home, so this is the time I get to cook.' (competing practical needs for stove time)
Turn 3 — Agent B: 'It's the smell. It's going right into my room.' / Turn 4 — Agent A: 'I use the fan. The window is open.' (disagreement about whether mitigation is sufficient)

Turn 5 — Agent B: 'It's not working. The smell is still coming into my room.' (contradicts A's claim the fan/window suffice) / Turn 6 — Agent C: 'And someone left this pan in the sink from last night.' (adds unwashed-pan cleanliness issue)

Turn 8 — Agent A: 'I'm not the only one who uses pans.' (defensive) / Turn 9 — Agent C: 'Okay. Then can we agree that whoever uses something, washes it?' (explicit proposal toward resolving the cleaning complaint)

Turn 10 — Agent D: 'Okay, but can we also talk about timing?... if I can't even get to the stove until nine, the washing up is also going to be late.' / Turn 11 — Agent A: 'So it's the smell, the washing up, and the time. What's the suggestion?' (timing issue remains active)

Turn 12 — Agent B: 'For me it's the smell. Can we just not cook things with such a strong smell on weeknights?' (requests behavioral restriction) / Turn 13 — Agent C: 'That pan from last night also adds to the smell. If we don't clean as we go, it makes it worse for everyone.' (reinforces cleaning as cause)

Turn 14 — Agent D: 'Right, but none of that solves the problem that I can't even get to the stove. Can we make a schedule? Or just agree that the kitchen needs to be free by a certain time?' / Turn 15 — Agent A: 'A schedule? How is that going to work? Are we booking time slots?' (proposal met with skepticism; timing conflict persists)

Turn 16 — Agent D: '...people try to be done by 8, so others can get a chance to cook before it gets too late.' / Turn 17 — Agent A: 'I'm working until 6 or 7. Being done by 8 is a bit hard.' (directly opposing practical constraints vs requested deadline)

substantive_insights: There are at least three distinct but related problems: smell, cleanliness, and stove access timing; they interact (unclean pans worsen smell; timing affects when washing can be done).
Mitigation (fan/window) is contested — B reports it as ineffective, so technical fixes alone are not trusted.

Proposals differ in cost and feasibility: cleaning rule is low-cost but needs buy-in; banning smelly cooking imposes lifestyle limits; scheduling raises coordination burdens given differing work patterns.
